statement: You receive integers x and n on one line. Print x raised to the power n. Use fast exponentiation: the answer for exponent n is the square of the answer for the floored half of n, times one extra x when n is odd. The base case is exponent 0, which answers 1. The exponent chain halves each call, so the whole computation takes a logarithmic number of multiplications.
constraints: The answer fits in a 64-bit integer.

example.why: The exponent falls along 10, 5, 2, 1, 0 and the squares rebuild 1024 in a handful of multiplies.

hint: Recurse once on the floored half and square the result - two recursive calls ruin the logarithm.
mistake: Forgetting the extra factor of x when n is odd; 2 to the 3 then returns 4.
